headline: Watch the concentration of revenue among a few water agencies and the execution of the company’s expansion and M&A plans.

matchedHeadings: offer for sale of 27,500,000 existing shares by way of private placement to bumiputera investors approved by the miti

data.summary: The IPO comprises a public issue of 121,000,000 shares (22.0% of enlarged share capital) and an offer for sale of 27,500,000 shares (5.0%) via private placement to Bumiputera investors approved by MITI, with estimated gross proceeds of approximately RM43.6 million from the public issue (accruing to the Company) and RM9.9 million from the offer for sale (accruing to Selling Shareholders).
data.grossProceeds: RM43.6 million from Public Issue; approximately RM9.9 million from Offer for Sale

useOfProceeds.purpose: Business expansion - Expansion of corporate office in Sarawak with a mini data centre
Business expansion - Expansion of IT operations
Business expansion - Expansion of West Malaysia branch office
Strategic investments, mergers and acquisitions opportunities

lines: The company supplies water technology solutions and intelligent asset management systems for water distribution, treatment, and other industries.
Its primary customers are water agencies in Sarawak (such as JBALB, Sibu Water Board) and businesses in hospitality, transportation, and construction.
It earns revenue through project-based contracts for system design, supply, installation, and ongoing maintenance or support services.

data.trend: The company demonstrated strong financial acceleration from FYE 2022 to FYE 2025, with revenue growing from RM29.1M to RM49.6M and profitability expanding dramatically. Gross profit and net margins more than doubled, driven by the high-margin intelligent asset management solutions segment.
highlights: Revenue increased 64% from FYE 2022 to FYE 2025
GP margin rose from 18.8% to 59.8% (more than doubled)
PAT margin surged from 8.0% to 38.2% (more than tripled)
Intelligent asset management solutions became the dominant high-margin growth driver

matchedHeadings: risk factors notwithstanding the prospects of our group as outlined in this prospectus, you should carefully consider the following risk factors that may have a significant impact on our future performance, in addition to all other relevant information contained elsewhere in this prospectus, before making an application for our ipo shares.

data.summary: The prospectus identifies key risks centered on customer concentration, project-based revenue volatility, intellectual property and cybersecurity exposure, credit and collection risks, execution of growth strategies, supply chain and subcontractor dependencies, and regulatory and licensing requirements.

themes.summary: The Group is heavily reliant on JBALB and other Sarawak water agencies, which contributed the majority of revenue, and the loss of any major customer could significantly impact financial performance.
Revenue, profit, and cash flow fluctuate due to the project-based nature of contracts, lack of long-term agreements, and dependency on securing new projects through competitive bidding.
The Group faces risks of IP infringement, source code leakage, hacking, and IT system breaches that could disrupt operations and harm reputation.
Delays or defaults in customer payments, including RM3.7 million in overdue receivables, may lead to bad debt write-offs and adversely affect cash flow.

themes.theme: Execution of Growth and Acquisition Strategies
themes.summary: Future growth depends on successfully executing business strategies, managing M&A opportunities, and integrating acquired businesses, with no guarantee of success.
Reliance on principals, suppliers, and subcontractors for IoT devices and project services exposes the Group to supply disruptions and cost overruns.
The Group must maintain various licenses and approvals, including UPKJ registration, and failure to do so could restrict participation in government procurements.

items.point: Heavy reliance on a small number of water agency customers (e.g., JBALB) for the majority of revenue.
items.why: Loss of any major customer could materially impact financial performance.

items.point: Project‑based revenue leads to volatility in earnings and cash flow.
items.why: Revenue, profit and cash flow fluctuate as contracts are won and completed on a competitive bidding basis.

items.point: Large portion of IPO proceeds (≈51%) allocated to general working capital and ~21% to strategic investments/M&A.
items.why: Future growth and capital allocation decisions will affect profitability and shareholder value.

items.point: Significant lock‑up on insider holdings (e.g., Wee Khiam Hui 37.2% of enlarged capital) limits immediate share supply.
items.why: Potential market impact when lock‑up expires and insiders may sell up to one‑third per year.

items.point: Related‑party purchases not on arm‑length terms (e.g., Advantage Focus) and personal guarantees for bank facilities.
items.why: These non‑arm‑length transactions could create conflicts of interest and affect financial obligations.

lockup.summary: A moratorium is imposed on the entire shareholdings of Specified Shareholders for 6 months from the date of admission to the Official List (First 6-Month Moratorium). Upon expiry, at least 45.0% of the total issued ordinary shares must remain under moratorium for another 6 months (Second 6-Month Moratorium). On expiry of the Second 6-Month Moratorium, Specified Shareholders may sell, transfer or assign up to a maximum of 1/3 per annum (on a straight-line basis) of the shares held under moratorium. The moratorium has been accepted by the Specified Shareholders, who provided written undertakings not to sell, transfer or assign their shareholdings during the moratorium period, and the restrictions are endorsed on the share certificates.

relatedParty.summary: The Group had several material related-party transactions including office premises rentals, subcontractor arrangements, ad-hoc purchases and supplies, computer and installation purchases, interest-free advances, and personal guarantees and third-party securities provided by directors and substantial shareholders for banking facilities. Some transactions were conducted on an arm's length basis while others were not. The Group has established procedures to ensure future related-party transactions are conducted on arm's length terms and has applied for the release of personal guarantees and third-party securities upon listing.
